subject: chemistry
title: Buffer Beacon: Resisting pH Change
welcome_lead: Build buffers with weak acid + conjugate base using Henderson-Hasselbalch.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on buffer composition and pH calculations.
final_note: You stabilised pH like a true biochemist.

concepts.def: Resists pH change on small acid/base addition.
Amount of acid/base before pH changes much.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mix weak acid HA with its conjugate base A- (e.g. ethanoic acid + sodium ethanoate). When acid added, A- neutralises. When base added, HA neutralises.

Best buffering when pH ≈ pKa (ratio [A-]/[HA] ≈ 1).

Use Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]).

Example: 0.10 mol HA + 0.20 mol A- with pKa 4.76 gives pH = 4.76 + log 2 = 5.06.

CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3 <-> H+ + HCO3-. Lungs and kidneys regulate concentrations.

Acidosis (pH<7.35) or alkalosis (pH>7.45) is dangerous. Buffer keeps blood pH near 7.4.
